newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil firm builds U.S soy crushing factory-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil firm builds U.S soy crushing factory-report.

text.p: Brazil's Incobrasa is building a soybean crushing facility in the U.S., local business daily Gazeta Mercantil said Monday.
In July the company will start operating the 2,000 tonne a day factory situated in Guilman, south of Chicago, Illinois, Gazeta said.
"It is a modest business which is not trying to rival the big multi-nationals," Incobrasa's owner Renato Ribeiro told Gazeta Mercantil.
"We intend to explore the North American market thoroughly. For the time being we are not thinking about any expansions," he added.
Ribeiro declined comment when contacted to confirm the report.
Incobrasa earlier this year sold its soybean processing and warehousing facilities in Rio Grande do Sul state to Brazilian food processor Santista Alimentos.
The firm reportedly received $75 million from the sale and will be investing around $30 million in the U.S. facility, Gazeta Mercantil said.
Almost all the output from the new factory will be directed to the North American market, it added.

Incobrasa was Brazil's largest exporter of soyoil in 1996, shipping 143,500 tonnes, and the third largest exporter of soymeal with 756,400 tonnes, according to the Brazilian Vegetable Oil Industries Association.
